strong_findings.citation: M. Kesden, M. Kamionkowski, "Galilean Equivalence for Galactic Dark Matter", Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 131303 (2006), arXiv:astro-ph/0606566
strong_findings.summary: If dark matter feels a stronger self-attraction than baryons, stars gain energy preferentially during tidal disruption and the trailing tidal stream is enhanced; the roughly equal streams of the Sagittarius dwarf challenge differences in acceleration above about 10%.
strong_findings.difference: A bound on an extra long-range attraction among dark matter only, not gated in velocity. For a gated force it applies at the satellite's relative speed; the momentum-gravity note (§6) maps it to ε ≲ O(1) (0.2–2.5) at v* = 120 km/s and finds it weaker than the Lyman-α forest. The record already uses it; listed here because its result weighs against the conjecture's required strength (ε > 1).

quotes.text: The Sgr dwarf galaxy is seen to have roughly equal streams, challenging models in which DM and baryons accelerate differently by more than 10%.

verified: Confirmed. A bound on an extra long-range attraction among dark matter; for a gated force it applies at the satellite's relative speed. The record already applies it (velocity-gated-gravity note §6).

related.citation: A. Loeb, N. Weiner, "Cores in Dwarf Galaxies from Dark Matter with a Yukawa Potential", Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 171302 (2011), arXiv:1011.6374
related.summary: Dark matter interacting through a Yukawa potential has a velocity-dependent cross-section that makes cores in dwarf galaxies while leaving systems with much larger velocity dispersion, such as clusters, unaffected.

related.citation: F. Bunchaft, S. Carneiro, "Weber-like interactions and energy conservation", Found. Phys. Lett. 10, 393 (1997), doi:10.1007/BF02764109, arXiv:gr-qc/9708047 (journal)

related.citation: J. Skolimowski, "Real-space analysis of Hatsugai-Kohmoto interaction", Phys. Rev. B 109, 165129 (2024), arXiv:2402.08557
related.summary: The Hatsugai–Kohmoto interaction is diagonal in momentum space, which makes it exactly solvable there; in real space it has infinite range, its strength not depending on the distance between the interacting particles.

related.citation: M. Costa, C. Creque-Sarbinowski, O. Simon, Z. J. Weiner, "Dark forces suppress structure growth", JCAP 06 (2026) 055, arXiv:2510.00098
related.summary: Minimal models of scalar-mediated attractive forces between dark-matter particles do not enhance the growth of unbiased tracers: the faster growth of the density contrast is cancelled by faster dilution of the background dark-matter density, and CMB-compatible versions suppress structure growth.

related.citation: P. Schuster, N. Toro, K. Zhou, "Interactions of Particles with 'Continuous Spin' Fields", JHEP 04 (2023) 010, arXiv:2303.04816
related.summary: For matter coupled to a scalar-like continuous-spin field, the leading velocity-dependent pair potential is L_int = (g²/4πr)[1 − (ρ²r²/32)(|vᵢ − vⱼ| − (vᵢ − vⱼ)·r̂)² + …] (eq. 129): a long-range interaction whose correction depends only on the relative velocity, vanishes for co-moving particles and for motion along the line joining them, and matters when ρvr ~ 1.

related.citation: R. Delbourgo, D. Lashmar, "Born reciprocity and the 1/r potential", Found. Phys. 38, 995 (2008), arXiv:0709.0776

related.citation: R. Lasenby, "Long range dark matter self-interactions and plasma instabilities", JCAP 11 (2020) 034, arXiv:2007.00667
related.summary: Dark matter interacting through a light vector mediator has a long-range self-interaction; coherent effects make small perturbations grow exponentially, as plasma instabilities do, at couplings far below the particle-by-particle limits. For velocity distributions with a single peak (such as an anisotropic Maxwellian) only magnetic instabilities exist.

related.citation: S. Kundu, P. Schuster, N. Toro, "First look at continuous spin gravity: Time delay signatures", Phys. Rev. D 113, 076017 (2026), arXiv:2503.03817
related.summary: First linearized formalism coupling spinless matter to gravity mediated by continuous-spin gravitons (spin scale ρ_g); it computes only the time-delay signatures of gravitational waves in an interferometer, at leading order in Newton's constant.

not_found_statements.statement: No paper found that proposes a long-range (1/r, gravity-like) attraction among dark-matter particles that acts only between particles moving at similar velocities, i.e. a relative-velocity gate W(|v − v′|/v*) on a gravity-like force, whether as dark-matter physics or as a modification of gravity. The closest are Delbourgo–Lashmar's Born-reciprocal term GmMΩ/|v − v′| among all masses (partial), the velocity-dependent correction of continuous-spin forces (Schuster–Toro–Zhou; scalar, threshold falling with distance), the Hatsugai–Kohmoto momentum-local interaction of infinite range (lattice electrons), and velocity-dependent self-interactions, which are collisional. This confirms and extends the record's earlier null search (review/momentum-gravity/run2/analyses/clumping.json, C18), which had missed Delbourgo–Lashmar.

No source found that states a long-range attraction among dark-matter particles acting only, or most strongly, between particles of similar velocity. The velocity-dependent gravity literature outside arXiv works at the velocity scale c or with absolute velocities, acts between all masses, and is offered as an alternative to dark matter or for perihelion precession. This covers Weber-like laws, Gerber-type fits (Gribkov), Arbab's generalized Newton law, Ghosh's inertial induction, Devasia's relative-velocity Weber model, Laletin's capture model and Hahn-Fine's measurement-induced attraction. None gates an attraction to small relative velocity at a scale like v* ~ 120 km/s, and none restricts it to dark matter. No Weber-type gravity paper applied to galaxy rotation curves was found (English and Portuguese searches). The closest remains Delbourgo-Lashmar 2008 (known: partial).

No lineage paper proposes a long-range attraction among dark-matter particles that acts only at small relative velocity. The velocity-dependent gravity of the Weber-Assis lineage weakens the attraction with relative radial speed on the scale of c and acts on all bodies (Assis, Relational Mechanics, Apeiron 2014, eq. 25.15, read in the author's PDF); the record already cites this lineage (notes/velocity-gated-gravity.md §3, Tisserand 1872). Ghosh's velocity-dependent inertial induction is applied, by its titles, to redshifts, solar-system anomalies and flat rotation curves; its abstracts were not reachable (unverified leads).

Holds, but the closest paper should be labelled related, not partial. Delbourgo and Lashmar's Omega/|v - v'| term depends only on relative velocity and exerts no force in position (their eq. 4; velocity-gated-gravity note §2). C7's defining feature, a 1/r attraction among dark matter switched by relative velocity, appears nowhere. My own searches (velocity-dependent long-range force; fifth force depending on relative velocity with dark matter; attraction at the same velocity with streams and long range; velocity-dependent gravitational constant for galaxies; interactions local in momentum and of infinite range applied to dark matter or gravity; attractive Hatsugai-Kohmoto; a web search for gravity depending on relative velocity among co-moving bodies; the citation graph of Delbourgo-Lashmar both ways, including Jarvis-Morgan 2005, which has no 1/p term) found nothing closer. A velocity criterion in superfluid dark matter (Berezhiani-Khoury: infall velocity against sound speed) concerns dissipation relative to the medium, a preferred-frame effect the note's §9 already covers, not a gate on a force between two bodies.
